name: Rosemary
description: An evergreen shrub with leaves like needles and pale blue flowers. It comes from the dry hills around the Mediterranean.

img.alt: Two sprigs of rosemary with narrow leaves like needles

growing.water: Little water, soil that drains well

harvest: Cut sprigs all year round, never more than a third of the plant.
steps: Plant it in the sunniest spot you have.
Use light soil that drains well; rosemary does not like wet roots.
Water only when the top of the soil feels dry.
In a cold winter, grow it in a pot and keep it in a bright place without frost.
Trim it after flowering to keep it bushy, but do not cut into old, bare wood.
uses: Roast it with potatoes and vegetables, or bake a sprig into bread.
Chop the leaves finely for marinades, soups and stews.
Tie a few sprigs together for a fragrant bundle in the kitchen.
Leave the pale blue flowers on the plant for the bees in spring.
